label: pp-fish-biomechanics-morphology
topic: Fish biomechanics, fin development and flying-fish experts, including near Boston
summary: Boston-area experts verified: Lauder (Harvard OEB/MCZ; fin and body mechanics; 3 verified recent papers), Harris (HMS/Boston Children's; fin development incl. a 2021 Current Biology flying-fish paper; 3 verified papers), Triantafyllou (MIT; biomimetic fish robots; only a 2000 paper verified, no recent fish paper found). Flying-fish gliding aerodynamics found is from outside Boston (Park and Choi 2010; Nguyen and Park 2023). Techet (MIT) searched, nothing verified. All collaborations are hypotheses.
lay_summary: We looked for scientists who study how fish fins work and grow. Near Boston, George Lauder at Harvard studies how fish swim, often with robot fish. Matthew Harris at Harvard Medical School studies the genes that set fin shape, including how flying fish got long wing-like fins. At MIT, Michael Triantafyllou builds robot fish. Each paper was checked against a public records database. Every idea of working together is only a guess, such as asking whether a simple unpowered glider model can show if a fin shape could glide at all.

findings.claim: Lauder is a Harvard OEB professor at the MCZ studying fish biomechanics and robotic aquatic models
Harris lab studies fish to understand genetic regulation of postembryonic development; HMS Genetics and Boston Children's Orthopedics
findings.evidence_quote: The Harris laboratory studies fish as a model to understand the genetic regulation of 'postembryonic' development

findings.claim: Harris-lab flying-fish paper: Daane et al. Current Biology 2021; DOI resolves in Crossref
findings.evidence_quote: Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes

findings.claim: Preprint of that work reports sequencing 35 beloniform species and that flying-fish pectoral fin length grows rapidly with body size
findings.source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2021.03.05.434157.full.pdf (search summary only; not read in full)

findings.claim: Triantafyllou holds the Doherty Professorship in Ocean Science and Engineering at MIT and pioneered biomimetic robots
findings.evidence_quote: He pioneered the development of science-driven biomimetic robots

findings.claim: Park and Choi 2010 measured aerodynamic characteristics of flying fish in gliding flight
findings.evidence_quote: Aerodynamic characteristics of flying fish in gliding flight

findings.claim: Hypothesis: a passive-glide surrogate could give Harris a fin-proportion to glide-performance map, testing whether fin-size changes found in flying fish help gliding
Hypothesis: the elimination framework could rule out fin shape and size combinations that cannot glide, for Lauder's fin-compliance and robot work
Hypothesis: a passive-glide surrogate could be a no-actuation baseline for MIT biomimetic fish robots and for tail-assisted glide models

key_claims.claim: Harris (Boston) co-authored a verified 2021 Current Biology paper on flying-fish fins
key_claims.evidence_quote: Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes

key_claims.claim: Lauder's lab has verified 2023-2024 fish swimming and fin papers
key_claims.evidence_quote: In-line swimming dynamics revealed by fish interacting with a robotic mechanism

key_claims.claim: The flying-fish gliding aerodynamics work found is outside Boston
key_claims.evidence_quote: Aerodynamic characteristics of flying fish in gliding flight
